title: Quantify permeability using on-a-chip models in high-throughput applications
protocol: Open FIJI software and load the images acquired previously.
Go to the directory where the data are stored.
Sort the data by "Date" by clicking on column heading label “Date”.
Select all the data by clicking Ctrl + A and drag them into FIJI.
Organize selected images into a stack using the "Image to Stack" option from the menu.
In the FIJI menu bar, select Image > Stacks > Images to Stack.
Choose a suitable name for the file in the “Image to Stack” menu.
Tick on “Use Titles as labels” in the “Image to Stack” menu.
Select "ok" to create the stack.
Inspect the stack for information about the total number of images and current image label.
Scroll through the stack using the scroll bar at the bottom left corner to change the image visualized.
Optional: In the FIJI menu bar, select Image → Stacks → Tools → Stack Sorter to reorder the images if necessary.
Convert the stack into an hyperstack in FIJI.
Select Image > Hyperstacks > Stack to Hyperstack… from the menu bar.
Fill in the “Convert to Hyperstack” menu with the appropriate number of channels (c), slices (z) and frames (t).
Select “Order” based on how the images are ordered (xyctz).
Check that each scroll bar contains the correct image by scrolling through them.
Open the align plugin.
Fill in the information to run the alignment.
Press “ok”.
Select an area which will be used by the plugin to align all the images.
Select “ok” in the “Align slices in stack” menu.
Choose a region including the bended part of the microfluidic chip for alignment.
Check that the images are aligned after alignment is performed.
Quantify fluorescence intensity in donor and receiver channel.
Load the ROI supplemented with this protocol.
Place the ROI above the phaseguide to select donor.
Open ROI manager.
Place the ROI below the phaseguide to select receiver area for quantification.
Run the quantification.
Select the measurement required for the analysis.
In the menu bar, select Analyze > Set Measurements…
Tick on “Mean gray value”, “Stack position”, and “Display label”.
Select "ok".
Select the area of interest in the donor channel.
Select the area of interest in the receiver channel.
Open the ROI file supplemented with this protocol by dragging it into FIJI menu bar.
Move the ROI above the PhaseGuide to quantify fluorescence intensity of the donor.
Zoom-in on the PhaseGuide to ensure it is excluded from the ROI.
In the menu bar, select Analyze > Tools > ROI Manager…
Select “Add [t]” and “ROI_BI” will appear in the window.
Move the ROI below the PhaseGuide.
Zoom in on the PhaseGuide to ensure it is excluded.
Select “Add” in the “ROI manager” menu and add a second ROI.
Relabel the first ROI as “ROI_BI_donor”.
Relabel the second ROI as “ROI_BI_receiver”.
Measure fluorescence intensities of both ROIs for all images in the hyperstack.
In the “ROI manager” window, select both ROIs.
Select More > Multi Measurement in the “ROI manager” menu.
Tick on Measure all 210 slices and One row per slice.
Click OK to proceed with measurements.
The “Results” panel will appear; save the file as csv by selecting File > Save as... > csv file.
Open Excel.
In the Excel menu bar, select File > Options.
In the "Add-ins" window, select "Go".
Tick on "Solver Add-in" and select "OK".
Load the data in the excel template file Papp_curve fitting.
Fill in with BI data the sheet in the excel template file.
Calculate the intensity ratio between fluorescence intensities of receiver and donor + receiver (Y) to fit experimental BI data.
In b, input donor fluorescence intensities in cells D23:D29.
In c, input receiver fluorescence intensities in cells F23:F29.
Set K and D equal to 1 in cells N22 and N23 respectively.
Calculate Y in cells H23:H29.
Fit the data in cells I23:I29.
Calculate chi square in cells J23:J29.
Open Solver function in Excel from Data > Solver menu.
In “Solver Parameters” menu, set "Set Objective" to $N$24 and choose Minimize option.
Specify variable cells as $N$22:$N$23 for Solver adjustment.
Tick on “Make Unconstrained Variables Non-Negative”.
Select solving method: GRG Nonlinear.
Click Solve.
Papp is calculated in cell N26.
Calculate Papp and sum chi square using the specified function.
Generate a graph plotting fluorescence intensity of donor (blue dots) and receiver (green dots) channel overtime on the left side.
Plot experimental data (blue dots) and fit (red line) obtained with solver Add-ins on the right side.
Check that neither the intensities of the receiver nor the donor decreases over time to ensure chip quality.
Duplicate the sheet and repeat steps from 8–13.a using data from other chips.
